name: Ahimelech
bio:
Ahimelech was the son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, grandson of Phinehas, and great-grandson of Eli — a priest of the LORD who appears earlier in 1 Samuel 14 under the name "Ahijah," present with Saul's army and wearing the ephod (1 Samuel 14:3). As confusion grew in the Philistine camp because of Jonathan's raid, Saul told him to bring the ark of God so he could inquire of the LORD, but with the battle pressing urgently, Saul soon told him to withdraw and led the army out to fight instead (1 Samuel 14:18-19).

When David fled from Saul, he came to Nob, where Ahimelech, trembling, came out to meet him and asked why he was alone with no men (1 Samuel 21:1). David lied that he was on a secret royal errand and asked for bread; Ahimelech had no ordinary bread, only the consecrated bread, which he gave him, along with the sword of Goliath, which David himself had taken (1 Samuel 21:2-9).

When Saul learned of this, he summoned Ahimelech and his father's whole priestly family, accusing them of conspiring with David; Ahimelech protested that he knew nothing of any rift between Saul and David, and that David was the king's own son-in-law and faithful servant (1 Samuel 22:11-15). Saul refused to listen and ordered all the priests of Nob put to death; when his own guards refused, he commanded Doeg the Edomite to do it, and Doeg killed eighty-five priests wearing the linen ephod, then put the entire town of Nob to the sword — men, women, children, and livestock alike (1 Samuel 22:16-19). Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped, fleeing to David; David, grief-stricken, admitted that seeing Doeg there that day, he should have known this would happen, saying, "I am responsible for the death of your father's whole family" (1 Samuel 22:20-23). Ahimelech's family, wiped out simply for an act of hospitality, stands as the darkest episode of Saul's paranoid, murderous final years. Centuries later, Jesus recalled this episode of David eating the consecrated bread, though he attributed it to "Abiathar the high priest" (Mark 2:26) — Ahimelech's son, who was not yet high priest at the time.
